sources: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/alerts (incl. Willow Fire Area Closure order 02-12-01-26-39)

values.note: Valley Loop $29, Sage Loop $30 a night (recreation.gov 2026-2028); the FS page says $30 per site. Two vehicles included; a third is $11 a night (boat/ATV trailers count as a vehicle). First-come sites are paid at a self-service fee tube (cash, check or money order). Firewood $10 a bundle from the host.

fees.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232387/rates (2026, 2027, 2028 Peak: VALL-STANDARD NONELECTRIC 29, SAGE-STANDARD NONELECTRIC 30) + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/white-star-campground ('$30 nightly fee per site. This includes parking for two vehicles. A third vehicle is an additional $11 per night'; 'A self-service fee tube is available'), read 2026-10-26

hookups.source: recreation.gov campsite catalog for 232387 (every public site STANDARD NONELECTRIC or TENT ONLY NONELECTRIC, no hookup attributes) + FS page (dump station closed; 'Everyone must go to the Leadville Sanitation Building for trailer dumping and water fill-ups'), read 2026-10-26

values.note: Sage (28) and Valley (21) loops are reservable: 46 standard sites (vehicle lengths 20-50 ft; three cap at 20 ft) and 3 tent-only sites. Ridge Loop's 16 first-come sites are not in the catalog, so their lengths are unknown. The count is the 62 standard sites. The stored 99 ft came from a management placeholder ('XXX').

sites.source: recreation.gov campsite catalog for 232387 (public sites: 46 STANDARD NONELECTRIC Max Vehicle Length 20-50, 3 TENT ONLY; all Back-in; loops SAGE 28, VALL 21; 18 MANAGEMENT 'XXX' records, one with Max Vehicle Length 99) + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232387 (notice 'the Ridge Loop is entirely First Come First Served and has 16 campsites'), read 2026-10-26

values.note: Drinking water from a hand pump. The campground's RV dump station is closed; dumping and water fill-ups at the Leadville Sanitation Building. Water, trash and host may be absent early and late in the season.

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/white-star-campground ('Vault toilets are located throughout the campground'; 'Potable water is available at this site. A hand pump is currently available'; 'THE RECREATIONAL VEHICLE (RV) DUMP STATION AT WHITE STAR IS CLOSED. Everyone must go to the Leadville Sanitation Building'; 'Services such as water, trash or a host may not be available during the early and late season'), last updated May 1, 2026, read 2026-10-26

values.note: Forest Service: generally open May through September; opening and closing dates are weather dependent.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/white-star-campground (Seasons of Use: 'The facility is generally open May through September. Opening and closing dates are weather dependent.'), read 2026-10-26

values.note: Sage and Valley loops are reservable on recreation.gov or 1-877-444-6777 at least four days ahead; Ridge Loop (16 sites) is always first-come, and the whole campground goes first-come after Labor Day (recreation.gov's 2027 first-come season Sept 6-18). Reservations need Friday and Saturday nights on weekends and three nights on holiday weekends; walk-ups are exempt. First-come sites must be occupied the first night. Reservation dates are recreation.gov's 2027 Peak season (2026: May 23 - Sept 19).

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/white-star-campground ('Call 1-877-444-6777 or visit recreation.gov at least four days in advance to make a reservation. A Friday and Saturday night minimum stay is required on weekends. A three-night minimum stay is required on holiday weekends. Walk-ups are exempt from the nightly minimum.'; 'Sage and Valley Loops have reservable sites, while Ridge Loop is first come, first served') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232387 (facility_rules maxConsecutiveStay 14) + /rates (2027 Peak 05-21 to 09-05; First-come, First-served Season 2027-09-06 to 09-18), read 2026-10-26

discounts.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/white-star-campground ('The Interagency Senior Pass and the Interagency Access Pass qualify for a 50% discount at concessionaire-run campsites'), read 2026-10-26

note: On the north shore of Twin Lakes Reservoir at the foot of Mount Elbert, in ponderosa pine and sage at 9,300 ft: Sage Loop has little shade, Valley and Ridge more pine and spruce. Boat ramp and angler fishing areas just down the road; the Continental Divide Trail passes by (Leadville RD, Pike-San Isabel NF). --Claude
summary: FS page (May 2026) + rec.gov facility/rates/catalog: confirmed $29-30 (2026-28), no electric. Max rig 99 -> 50 (99 was a management 'XXX' record; public sites 20-50 ft), count 49 -> 62 (46 reservable standard + Ridge Loop's 16 first-come). Added no water/sewer, back-in only, vault toilets, hand-pump water, season note (May-Sept, no dates), 4-day lead, weekend 2-night / holiday 3-night minimum, 14-night max, some_sites FCFS, booking.season May 21 - Sept 5 (2027), senior/access 50%. Dump station closed (note). Pin ~130 m from the per-site centroid. Willow Fire closure (Oct-Dec 2026) covers the Mount Massive side north of Halfmoon Creek, not Twin Lakes. Note: dropped the 'Turquoise/Twin Lakes' and count/length/reservable restatements. The brief placed White Star on Turquoise Lake; FS and recreation.gov put it on Twin Lakes Reservoir.
